design_implications: Pin the Admin API to 2026-07 in an environment variable (for example SHOPIFY_API_VERSION). Call POST https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/api/2026-07/graphql.json with the X-Shopify-Access-Token header. Plan to move to 2026-10 or 2027-01 within about 12 months. The webhook payload version is set in the Dev Dashboard app version, not per subscription.

Recommended COD path is orderCreate. Example variables: {order: {lineItems: [{variantId, quantity, priceSet: {shopMoney: {amount, currencyCode: "COP"}}, requiresShipping: true}], customer: {toAssociate: {id}} or {toUpsert: {phone: "+57...", firstName, lastName}}, shippingAddress: {firstName, lastName, address1, address2, city, provinceCode, countryCode: "CO", zip?, phone}, shippingLines: [{title, priceSet}], financialStatus: PENDING, transactions: [{gateway: "Cash on Delivery (COD)", kind: SALE, status: PENDING, amountSet}], taxesIncluded: true, sourceIdentifier: <conversation/order key>, tags: ["whatsapp", "contraentrega"], note, customAttributes}, options: {inventoryBehaviour: DECREMENT_OBEYING_POLICY, sendReceipt: false, sendFulfillmentReceipt: false}}. Before going live, test on a dev store that the order shows 'Payment pending', has COD in paymentGatewayNames, and decrements stock. Also check that the tax totals are right.

Use the draft path (draftOrderCalculate, then draftOrderCreate, then draftOrderComplete with paymentPending: true) if you want Shopify to compute taxes, automatic discounts and shipping from the catalog. That costs two write calls and the write_draft_orders scope. draftOrderCalculate is useful on its own: the agent can quote an exact total before the customer says 'sí, confirmo'.
Recheck price, availableForSale and inventoryQuantity for the chosen variant right before creating the order. The offer message may be hours old. Send the price you validated as priceSet.

Token handling in Next.js: keep SHOPIFY_CLIENT_ID and SHOPIFY_CLIENT_SECRET server-side only. Mint a token through the client-credentials grant, cache it in memory or in Prisma until shortly before it expires (24h), use a mutex so concurrent requests mint only once, and re-mint and retry once on a 401. Never put the token or secret into the model's context.

Setup checklist: create the app in the Dev Dashboard under the same Organization that owns the DV Digital store. Release a version with the scopes read_products, read_inventory, read_locations, write_orders (write_orders implies read_orders), read_customers, write_customers, plus read_fulfillments and write_draft_orders if needed. Install it on the store. If the token request returns shop_not_permitted, fall back to the OAuth authorization-code flow with an expiring offline token and refresh token.

Check the store plan and configure protected customer data access (name, phone, address, email) on the app. On lower-tier plans, PII reads (customer lookup, order addresses in webhooks) may come back null or blocked, and the agent would lose customer context.

Webhook route (app/api/shopify/webhooks/route.ts): read the raw body with await req.text() before any JSON parsing. Compute base64 HMAC-SHA256 with the client secret and compare it to X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 using crypto.timingSafeEqual. Deduplicate on X-Shopify-Webhook-Id in Prisma. Reply 200 quickly and process in a queue. Subscribe to orders/create, orders/updated, orders/cancelled, fulfillments/create and fulfillments/update so status updates go back to the customer on WhatsApp.

Idempotency: orderCreate has no idempotency key. Store a pending-order row in Prisma with a unique key. Put that key in sourceIdentifier and in a tag, and before any retry query orders(query: "source_identifier:KEY") so a timeout never produces two COD shipments.

Phone handling: normalise WhatsApp wa_id or phone to E.164 (+57 plus 10 digits for Colombian mobiles). Look up with customerByIdentifier(phoneNumber), then use customer.toAssociate. Handle the 'phone already taken' userError. Read defaultPhoneNumber.phoneNumber, not the deprecated Customer.phone.

Colombian addresses: keep a static table mapping department names and aliases (for example 'Bogotá', 'Valle') to Shopify provinceCode (DC, VAC, ANT, CUN, ATL, SAN, ...), taken from Shopify/worldwide CO.yml. Have the agent collect city, department, street with number (address1, for example 'Calle 28 # 13A-15'), apartment and barrio (address2), and an optional 6-digit postal code. Send provinceCode and countryCode, not the deprecated province and country fields.

Rate limits and catalog: sync products, variants and stock into Prisma. Refresh on PRODUCTS_UPDATE and INVENTORY_LEVELS_UPDATE webhooks plus a periodic reconcile, instead of calling Shopify on every WhatsApp message. Read extensions.cost.throttleStatus and back off on THROTTLED.

Consent for the 50k-number base: keep your own consent ledger. On 2026-07 you can also mirror opt-in and opt-out into Shopify with customerWhatsAppMarketingConsentUpdate (state SUBSCRIBED or UNSUBSCRIBED, optInLevel, updatedAt), and listen to CUSTOMERS_WHATS_APP_MARKETING_CONSENT_UPDATE.

Testing: dev and trial stores allow at most 5 orderCreate calls per minute. Set test: true on the order and transaction where appropriate, and never let the agent create orders without the explicit confirmation step.
open_questions: Dropi (and any other Colombian COD fulfillment app): does it import every order from orders/create, or does it filter on gateway name ('Cash on Delivery (COD)' vs a Spanish label), tags, sourceName or financial status? Does it need exact DANE city names? dropi.co and apps.shopify.com were blocked, so I could not check.
orderCreate with variantId: does requiresShipping come from the variant despite the schema default of false? A community implementation claims it does. Test it, or always send true.

Does a SALE transaction with status PENDING and gateway 'Cash on Delivery (COD)' make an orderCreate order look and behave exactly like a checkout COD order ('Payment pending', 'Mark as paid' available, COD shown in paymentGatewayNames)? Or is financialStatus PENDING with no transaction better?
Does orderCreate compute Colombian IVA automatically, or must taxesIncluded and taxLines be sent explicitly? The schema only describes the manual fields.
Which Shopify plans exactly allow PII access for Dev Dashboard or custom apps? PostHog quotes 'Shopify, Advanced, and Plus'; Databricks says 'Advanced and Plus'. Which plan is DV Digital's store on?

Is DV Digital's production store in the same Dev Dashboard Organization as the app it will create? If the store was created outside the Dev Dashboard, will the client-credentials grant fail with shop_not_permitted? Needs a live test.
Exact current per-plan GraphQL Admin rate limits (shopify.dev/docs/api/usage/limits could not be opened) and any extra order-creation throttle on paid stores.
Exact end-of-support date for 2025-10 and the release date of 2026-10 (the versioning page could not be opened).
Does a Dev Dashboard app that is not a sales channel have its custom sourceName (for example 'whatsapp') accepted and shown, or ignored or rejected?
resultado.tool_problems:
WebFetch to shopify.dev, help.shopify.com, www.shopify.com, apps.shopify.com, community.shopify.dev and dropi.co returned EGRESS_BLOCKED. WebSearch was unusable: the session's budget of 200 searches was already spent. The request to inspect the proxy status was denied. Workaround: I downloaded Shopify's official npm packages from registry.npmjs.org, which was reachable:
- @shopify/dev-mcp 1.15.4 (published 2026-09-18). It bundles the Admin GraphQL introspection schemas for 2025-10 through 2026-10 and unstable, with the shopify.dev reference descriptions, per-field requiredAccess and offline_scopes data, and supported-versions-schema.json.
- @shopify/shopify-api 15.0.0 and @shopify/worldwide 0.7.10.
I also read Shopify-owned GitHub repos through raw.githubusercontent.com (worldwide, shopify-app-js, lighthouse-ci-action, claude-for-commerce-examples, shopify-api-ruby) and used GitHub code search. Every shopify.dev fact above is quoted from those schema files, not from shopify.dev pages. Canonical shopify.dev URLs are left out of the sources because I could not open them. Rate-limit numbers per plan, the protected-customer-data plan rules and Dropi behaviour rest on secondary or third-party sources, or are unverified, and are marked medium confidence or listed as open questions.

resultado.summary:
This covers the operational facts for a WhatsApp bot that takes cash-on-delivery (COD, "contra entrega") orders in Colombia and creates them in Shopify and Dropi. Web access was badly limited. WebSearch had no calls left (200/200 used), and WebFetch was blocked for every non-GitHub site I tried, including datos.gov.co, DANE, CRC, DIAN, Wikipedia, shopify.dev, the Shopify help center and App Store, dropi.co, releasit.com, easysell.io, servientrega.com and the OSM wiki. I therefore rebuilt the picture from primary data files hosted on GitHub: Shopify's own open-source `worldwide` address data, Google libphonenumber (latest release 23 Sep 2026), Unicode CLDR, and a mirror of Dropi's own WooCommerce plugin (v4.7.3). I added a May-2026 mirror of the DANE DIVIPOLA dataset and code from third-party Colombian COD integrators (Releasit form configs, Dropi API clients, carrier web-service payloads, carrier delivery-issue lists).

Main findings:
(1) **Official place list.** DIVIPOLA (datos.gov.co dataset gdxc-w37w) has 1,122 entries: 1,103 municipios including Bogotá D.C., 18 áreas no municipalizadas and 1 "isla", across 33 department codes. 66 municipio names repeat across departments (151 municipios in total), so the bot must always capture both departamento and municipio.
(2) **Three systems name places differently.** Shopify models Colombia as 33 zones with "Bogotá, D.C." (code DC) separate from Cundinamarca, the postal code only "recommended", and supports a neighborhood (barrio) field in its extended format. Dropi's own plugin data lists 32 departments with its own codes, places "Bogota" under Cundinamarca, and uses unaccented city names with suffixes like "ARGELIA (A)". Dropi also returns names normalized ("BOGOTA / CUNDINAMARCA"). A mapping table is therefore mandatory.
(3) **Dropi order API.** Dropi's plugin creates orders with POST {api}/integrations/orders/myorders, a `dropi-integration-key` header, and fields name, surname, dir, state, city, phone, client_email, total_order and products. It sets rate_type "CON RECAUDO" for COD and status "PENDIENTE CONFIRMACION". It sends no zip code or cédula for Colombia. Integrators report that the API needs an IP allowlist and wants the phone as a 10-digit national number. They also report that orders from Shopify reach Dropi after about 15 minutes, and some never arrive.
(4) **Carriers key destinations by DANE code.** Coordinadora's guide web service takes a DANE code for ciudad_destinatario; Servientrega's quote uses 8-digit DANE codes such as 76001000.
(5) **Addresses.** The format is "<vía> <número> # <cruce>-<placa>" (for example "Calle 5 # 17-28"). Official abbreviations come from DIAN and IGAC (Carrera is CR in DIAN, KR in IGAC). Common extras: AP apartamento, TO torre, CON conjunto, BRR barrio, VRD vereda.
(6) **Why COD deliveries fail.** Typical carrier delivery issues ("novedades") are: incomplete or unlocatable address (the fix is barrio plus a reference point, "sobre todo en la región Caribe"), rural areas with no coverage (vereda, finca, corregimiento), nobody home after 2 attempts, the customer has no cash or cancels, and the customer wants to open the parcel before paying.
(7) **Phones.** Mobiles are +57 and 10 digits starting with 3. Landlines are 10 digits: 60 + a regional digit + 7 digits (601 Bogotá, 604 Medellín, 602 Cali, 605 Barranquilla...).
(8) **Prices.** es-CO formatting uses "." for thousands and "," for decimals, and CLDR gives COP 0 decimal places. Intl.NumberFormat('es-CO', {style: 'currency', currency: 'COP'}) prints "$ 89.900" with a non-breaking space.
(9) **Tone.** "Ustedeo" (using usted even with friends and family) is strong in Bogotá and the Andean interior. Voseo is common in the Paisa region and Cali, and the Caribbean coast and young urban speakers lean toward "tú".

Confidence is medium or low wherever I could not open the official page directly.

claims.claim: A Colombian urban address is '<tipo de vía> <número principal> # <número de la vía que cruza> - <placa>'. In 'Calle 5 # 17-28' the door is on Calle 5, about 28 m from Carrera 17. Letters are glued to the number ('4A'), 'Bis' follows the number, and cardinal suffixes (Sur, Norte, Este, Oeste) come last ('Calle 4A Bis B Sur'). Official abbreviations (DIAN/MUISCA) are CL Calle, CR Carrera (the IGAC/Bogotá cadastre uses KR), AV Avenida, AC Avenida Calle, AK Avenida Carrera, DG Diagonal, TV Transversal and CIR Circular (IGAC: CQ). Informal forms such as Cll, Cra, Kra, Diag and Trans are common. Swapping Calle and Carrera sends the parcel elsewhere; an address without '# cruce - placa' identifies a street, not a door.

claims.claim:
The recurring carrier delivery issues on Dropi COD shipments, as compiled from Coordinadora, Interrapidísimo and Envía status specifications, are:
- 'DIRECCIÓN INCOMPLETA' and 'NO SE LOCALIZA DIRECCIÓN'. The fix is to reconfirm the full address with barrio, city and a reference point, 'sobre todo en la región Caribe'.
- 'SE VISITA, NO SE LOGRA ENTREGA' (nobody home). After 2 attempts the customer must be contacted, and a third attempt needs their authorization; after 2 failed attempts Coordinadora holds the parcel at an office.
- 'EL DESTINATARIO NO CANCELA EL VALOR A RECAUDAR' (the customer has no cash).
- 'PEDIDO CANCELADO' (the customer no longer wants it).
- 'DESTINATARIO SOLICITA OTRA DIRECCIÓN'.
- 'DESTINATARIO SOLICITA INVENTARIO' (wants to open the parcel before paying).
- 'RECLAME EN OFICINA': Interrapidísimo gives 15 calendar days to collect at the office.
I found no primary source with Colombian COD return-rate figures.

claims.claim: COD coverage is not universal. Carriers flag 'SECTOR DE LA POBLACIÓN DE DESTINO QUE NO SE CUBRE' for corregimientos, fincas, veredas and 'zonas rojas', where no fincas or veredas are served, and redirect the parcel to an office for pickup. claims.claim: Colombian numbers use country code 57. Mobiles are 10-digit national numbers starting with 3 (example 3211234567; current prefixes include 300-305, 310-319, 320-324, 333, 350-351 and 370), formatted '321 1234567' and written internationally as +57 321 1234567. The WhatsApp form is 573211234567. When parsing, libphonenumber also strips a leading national prefix 0 and old carrier-selection codes (03, 05, 07, 09, 0444, 0456), which covers inputs like '0573…' or '03 300…'. The metadata comes from the libphonenumber release of Sep 23, 2026, with Colombia's data last touched in v9.0.6 (May 2025).

claims.claim: Colombian fixed lines are now 10-digit national numbers: '60' + a 1-digit region + 7 digits (example 6012345678), formatted '601 2345678'. The region digits are 601 Bogotá/Cundinamarca, 602 Cali/Valle region, 604 Medellín/Antioquia, 605 Barranquilla/Caribbean, 606 Pereira/Eje Cafetero, 607 Cúcuta/Bucaramanga and 608 Ibagué/Villavicencio. A number starting 60 is a landline and cannot receive WhatsApp in the usual case, so the bot should ask for a mobile. The regulator's text (CRC) and the exact start date (believed to be 1 September 2021) could not be verified here.

claims.claim: Colombian Spanish (es-CO) number formatting uses '.' for thousands and ',' for decimals, and the COP symbol is '$'. CLDR's currency pattern is '¤ #,##0.00', but CLDR gives COP 0 fraction digits. Intl.NumberFormat('es-CO', {style: 'currency', currency: 'COP'}).format(89900) therefore returns '$ 89.900', where the space is a non-breaking U+00A0 (tested on Node 22.22.2 / ICU 78.2 / CLDR 48). Shopify stores COP with 2 decimals: a storefront JSON showed "price":18900000 (minor units) for a $189.000 product, and a Releasit offer displayed '$99.700,00'. In chat, show whole pesos ('$ 89.900') and keep integer arithmetic in the database.

claims.claim: Colombian Spanish is known for 'ustedeo', using 'usted' even with friends and family. It is strongest in Bogotá, the Cundiboyacense highlands, Santander and Tolima/Huila; Cundinamarca and Boyacá also use 'sumercé'. Voseo is common in the Paisa region (Antioquia, Eje Cafetero) and Cali/Valle. The Caribbean coast and younger urban speakers increasingly use 'tú'. A default of respectful 'usted' that switches to the customer's own register is the safe choice for sales chat; this recommendation is my inference, since no e-commerce-specific source was found.
claims.as_of: undated Wikipedia mirror (likely several years old)

sources.title: Mirror of Wikipedia 'Colombian Spanish'
sources.quote: The Spanish of a large part of the population in Colombia, especially in Bogota, is known for the use of "usted" ... between friends, family members ... Currently, though, younger speakers, especially in urban areas, tend to use "tú". ... voseo ... in the Paisa region and the Valle del Cauca, and the use of "su merced" ... in Cundinamarca and Boyacá.

design_implications: Seed a `Municipio` table from DIVIPOLA gdxc-w37w: 1,122 rows. Columns: 5-digit code, cod_dpto, name, type, lat/lon. Add mapping columns: Shopify provinceCode (DC for 11001, CUN for 25xxx, etc.), Dropi department id/name and Dropi city id/name/cod_dane, filled from Dropi's department and trajectory/bycity (CON RECAUDO) endpoints and refreshed daily. Match names accent- and case-insensitively, strip Dropi suffixes like '(A)', and review unmatched rows by hand.
Map Bogotá explicitly. Shopify: provinceCode 'DC', city 'Bogotá'. Dropi, per its plugin data: state 'CUNDINAMARCA', city 'BOGOTA'. Carriers: DANE code 11001 or 11001000.

The address conversation needs these slots: departamento → municipio (ask for the department whenever the city name is one of the 66 duplicated names, or always), dirección (vía + número + # + cruce - placa), complemento (torre/apto/casa/interior/conjunto), barrio (required), punto de referencia (strongly recommended, required on the Caribbean coast), full name (nombre + apellido, since Dropi needs name and surname separately), and a 10-digit mobile. Treat cédula as optional unless the Dropi account or carrier requires it.

Build an address normalizer that accepts DIAN, IGAC and informal abbreviations (Cl/Cll, Cra/Kra/Kr/CR/KR, Av/AC/AK, Dg/Diag, Tv/Trans, Cir/CQ) and '#', 'No.', 'N°' or 'número'. Output one canonical form, e.g. 'Calle 20 # 7-15, Torre 2 Apto 301, Barrio X'. Reject or flag addresses missing the '# cruce - placa' part. Flag rural tokens (vereda, finca, km, corregimiento) and offer office pickup or decline COD.

Map to Shopify's orderCreate fields as follows: address1 = normalized vía + placa; address2 = complemento + ' – Barrio ' + barrio (+ reference, or put the reference in the order note); city = municipio; provinceCode = Shopify zone code; countryCode = CO; zip = optional (Shopify only 'recommends' it). Also write barrio, cédula and the DIVIPOLA code into note_attributes and metafields for downstream tools.

Phones: parse with libphonenumber-js, region CO. Accept inputs like '300 123 4567', '3001234567', '+57 300…', '57300…', '(+57) 300-123-4567' and '0 300…'. Store E.164 (+573001234567) for Shopify and WhatsApp, and send the 10-digit national number (3001234567) to Dropi. If the number starts with 60 it is a landline: ask for a mobile.

Prices: store COP as integers and render with Intl.NumberFormat('es-CO', {style: 'currency', currency: 'COP', maximumFractionDigits: 0}), which gives '$ 89.900'. Watch for Shopify's 2-decimal minor units in product JSON (18900000 = $189.000).

Coverage check before quoting: resolve the municipio's Dropi city under rate_type 'CON RECAUDO'. If it is missing, say COD delivery isn't available there, or offer office pickup. Keep a department blocklist as a fast pre-filter (typical exclusions: Amazonas, Chocó, Guainía, Guaviare, Putumayo, San Andrés, Vaupés, Vichada), but let the API decide.

The confirmation step should send one summary message: product/variant/qty, total in cash on delivery, name, mobile, full address with barrio and reference, department/municipio, and an estimated delivery window. Add explicit buttons ('Sí, confirmo' / 'Corregir'). Store the confirmation timestamp and message id as proof. Only then create the order.

Keep the order in a draft or 'PENDIENTE CONFIRMACION' state until the customer confirms, and use shop_order_id or an internal id as the idempotency key. After creating a Dropi order, verify it with GET orders/myorders/{id}, not the list, to avoid duplicates.

If you rely on Dropi's Shopify app to import bot-created orders, add reconciliation: record every Shopify order the bot creates and alert if it hasn't shown up in Dropi after about 45 minutes. Tag bot orders distinctly (e.g. 'whatsapp-bot', 'cod'), because Releasit-based tools filter on 'releasit_cod_form'.

If you call Dropi's Integrations API directly from Next.js, you need a fixed egress IP (static-IP proxy or a VPS worker). Default serverless egress IPs won't pass Dropi's allowlist, and production access requires Dropi's enablement.

Handle delivery issues after the sale: poll or receive Dropi status updates and, on DIRECCIÓN INCOMPLETA, NO SE LOCALIZA or SE VISITA NO SE LOGRA ENTREGA, message the customer on WhatsApp (outside the 24-hour window this needs an approved template) asking for the corrected address or a delivery time. Remind them to have the exact cash ready and that the package is paid before opening, if that is the carrier's policy.

Tone: default to warm 'usted' ('¿Me regala su nombre completo, por favor?', '¡Con gusto!', 'a la orden'), mirror 'tú' if the customer uses it, and avoid Spain or Brazil-isms. Keep prices in Colombian format and name cities the way Colombians do (e.g. 'Bogotá', 'Medellín').

Per-carrier COD coverage by municipality (Servientrega, Interrapidísimo, Coordinadora, Envía, TCC), COD value limits, and whether each carrier lets customers open the parcel before paying: no primary carrier documentation was reachable.

missed.claim: Colombian data-protection law is the binding legal constraint, beyond WhatsApp's own terms. Ley Estatutaria 1581 de 2012 and Decreto 1377 de 2013 (now in Decreto 1074 de 2015) require prior, express and informed authorization from each person, which the company must be able to prove, before their data is processed for marketing. They also require a published data-treatment policy and a way for people to revoke consent, and the SIC can impose fines. The 50,000+ numbers can be used for promotions only for people who authorized marketing contact from DV Digital. Numbers that were bought or scraped cannot be used legally. From my knowledge only; not verified this session because network access was blocked.

Colombia's Ley 2300 de 2023 ('Dejen de fregar') limits consumer contact by businesses, which I believe includes advertising messages as well as debt collection. As I remember it: contact only through channels the consumer authorized, only on weekdays 7:00-19:00 and Saturdays 8:00-15:00 (none on Sundays or holidays), and no more than once a week per channel. If this applies to WhatsApp promo messages and group posts, the posting schedule and frequency need to be designed around it. From memory; confirm with the SIC and the text of the law.

The WhatsApp Business Solution terms changed from 15 January 2026. They ban general-purpose AI assistants on the Business API, but AI used for a business's own customer support or commerce (like DV Digital's order agent) stays allowed. Keep the agent scoped to the store's products, orders and support. From memory; confirm the current wording.

Sending outside the 24-hour window, such as order-confirmation or delivery updates for COD orders, needs approved templates. Meta has charged per delivered template since 1 July 2025, at rates set by the recipient's country (Colombia +57). Utility templates are free only inside the customer-service window. Marketing templates count toward per-user marketing frequency caps, the number's quality rating and its messaging-limit tier. Budget and design order notifications around this. From memory; confirm the current Colombia rate card.

WhatsApp's Commerce Policy and Business Policy restrict what can be sold (for example some health products, supplements, weapons, adult items and digital services). Reported violations can lead to catalog rejection or restriction of the number, separate from spam bans. Check DV Digital's product list against the Commerce Policy before advertising products through the API number. From memory; not verified this session.

verdicts.corrected_claim: The Cloud API does have a Groups API. Messages go to a group through the Messages API with recipient_type 'group' and the group ID in 'to'. Groups are created per business phone number and return an invite link, and join_approval_mode can be approval_required or auto_approve. Meta's docs, as quoted by the pywa SDK, describe groups as an invite-only experience joined through an invite link. However, Meta's own OpenAPI spec (updated August 2026) also lists a POST /{group_id}/participants endpoint named 'Add Group Participants' (max 8 per call), and the webhooks include a group_add_participants event. So 'no endpoint to add someone directly' is not clearly true; treat it as uncertain. The spec's description of that endpoint looks copy-pasted ('...to remove'), and pywa (v4.5.0, 24 Sep 2026) only implements remove. The OBA requirement, the exclusion of Business app and Multi-solution numbers, and the Calling API exclusion could not be checked against a primary page from here.
verdicts.evidence: developers.facebook.com, whatsapp.com and every secondary site were blocked by the egress proxy (403), and the web-search budget was used up. Primary evidence came from Meta's own OpenAPI repo (github.com/facebook/openapi, business-messaging-api_v23.0.yaml, last commit 2026-08-11). It shows: MessageRequest recipient_type enum [individual, group], with 'to' described as 'The recipient's phone number for individual messages, and group-id for group message'; POST /{Phone-Number-ID}/groups 'Create a new group and get an invite link'; POST /{group_id}/invite_link; join_approval_mode approval_required/auto_approve; and POST /{group_id}/participants 'Add Group Participants' with participants maxItems 8. pywa's docs (github.com/david-lev/pywa) say: 'Groups are an invite-only experience where participants join using a group invite link you send them', and pywa implements only remove_group_participants. The core conclusion stands either way: the API cannot run large promo groups.

verdicts.corrected_claim: Messages webhooks carry a business-scoped user ID (BSUID) in user_id, and a separate parent-portfolio-scoped ID (parent_user_id) exists when enabled. Meta's spec says the BSUID is 'Omitted when business-scoped user IDs are not enabled for the business', so it is not universal. BSUIDs are NOT permanent: when a user changes phone number they get a new BSUID for every business, and Meta sends user_changed_number or user_changed_user_id system webhooks (with previous_user_id since August 2026) so businesses can link old and new IDs. Some users are known only by username, and Meta notes the spec's required 'from' phone number is wrong for those users, so a business may receive messages with no phone number. The 'since April 2026' date and the 'contacts block omitted on failure' detail could not be verified.
verdicts.evidence: Primary evidence from Meta's own facebook/openapi repo, commits a89c18a and e96a1c9 (11 August 2026, authored by a meta.com engineer). They say: 'a phone number change does not carry the LID over -- the new number gets a new LID, and therefore a new BSUID for every business the consumer talks to'; 'contacts who know the consumer solely by username get a LID-change notification with no number in it'; 'BaseMessageProperties marks `from` required, which is wrong for username-only users'; and 'BSUIDs are expected to rotate for other reasons later -- a country-code change, or integrity-driven rotation'.

missed.claim: Colombian consumer-contact law applies on top of Meta's opt-in rules. Ley 1581 de 2012 (habeas data, enforced by the SIC) requires prior, express, informed authorization to process personal data for marketing. Ley 2300 de 2023 restricts commercial and advertising contact to channels the consumer authorized, within set hours (weekdays about 7:00–19:00, Saturdays about 8:00–15:00, not on Sundays or holidays) and no more than once a week. A 50,000-number blast or daily promo pushes could breach it even if Meta allows them. No primary source could be opened from this environment, so this needs checking against the law texts or a Colombian lawyer.

Syncing the Shopify catalog to a Meta catalog would let customers pick products and send a cart inside WhatsApp. That fits the 'never visit the website' goal, and the agent then only needs to confirm name, address and COD before creating the Shopify order.

resultado.summary: Short version: WhatsApp's official API cannot run big promo groups, so DV Digital has to split the system in two. (1) Broadcast: groups of hundreds of people exist only in the consumer app and the WhatsApp Business app. Meta's official Groups API allows at most 8 participants per group, requires an Official Business Account, and does not allow interactive or commerce messages inside groups. Automating large groups (auto-posting, link-rotator tools such as SendFlow) means linking the phone as a device through an unofficial client. WhatsApp's Terms and Messaging Guidelines prohibit that ("unofficial clients, bulk messaging, auto-messaging"), and the libraries themselves warn that you can be blocked. The legal paths for broadcasting are a WhatsApp Channel, or announcement-only groups posted by a person, and Meta's opt-in and opt-out rules apply either way. Meta's Business Messaging Policy covers the Business app as well as the API. It allows contact only with people who gave their number and opted in, and it lets Meta restrict senders after blocks and reports. (2) Private sales chat: this belongs on a separate official Cloud API number. Meta provides tools that identify the product without guessing: wa.me links with prefilled text carrying an offer code (QR/short-link API: up to 140 characters, 2,000 per number, no analytics from Meta), `context.referred_product` when someone taps "Message business" on a catalog product, and `order` webhooks from the native cart. Automated replies are allowed inside the 24-hour window, but only with "prompt, clear, and direct escalation paths", for example handing the chat to a human. A store's own sales agent is allowed under the Jan/Mar 2026 terms, which ban only general-purpose "AI Providers". In Colombia the address has to be collected as free text or with WhatsApp Flows, because Meta's address messages work only in India. The new business-scoped user IDs (BSUID) mean the phone number may not arrive in webhooks, so the agent must ask for the delivery phone explicitly. Measurement: Meta gives no analytics for short links, so clicks have to be tracked with a DV Digital redirect link plus the offer code. Joins and leaves should be stored as an event log. Hard numbers on posting frequency and churn are scarce. The only real data points found come from public GitHub repos: one Latin American launch campaign where 22,741 of 100,849 people who joined left, and one Brazilian analysis where people who joined the group converted 2.52x more (0.70% vs 0.28%), which may partly reflect who chose to join. Recommendations on posting frequency (2–3 posts a week, or 5–10 offers a day) are practitioner opinion, not evidence. Major caveat: web search was used up and nearly every official domain was blocked. Meta docs were read from a GitHub scrape of developers.facebook.com dated 2026-06-28 and from Meta's own facebook/openapi repo. WhatsApp legal texts came from OpenTermsArchive copies on GitHub, the Messaging Guidelines and Business Messaging Policy dated Sept 23 2026.

design_implications: Run two separate phone numbers and never mix them. (a) The broadcast surface is a WhatsApp Channel or admin-only community/announcement groups on the WhatsApp Business app, posted by a person. Automating group posting with an unofficial client is a ban risk the owner must explicitly accept. (b) The sales number runs on the official Cloud API with the Claude agent. The AI agent must never run on an unofficial or linked-device number, and must never reply inside groups.

Do not bulk-add the 50k numbers to groups and do not bulk-DM them from the app. That breaks the opt-in and 'at scale in an unauthorized manner' rules and exposes every member's phone number to the others. Invite people with a join link. Where the leads have documented opt-in to receive offers from DV Digital, the invite can go out as an approved marketing template from the Cloud API number. Otherwise, get their permission again first. Record the source and timestamp of every consent in a Consent table.

Every offer post links to a DV Digital redirect, e.g. https://<domain>/o/<OFFERCODE>?src=<groupId|channel>&utm_source=whatsapp&utm_medium=grupo&utm_campaign=<campaign>. The redirect logs the click, then sends a 302 to https://wa.me/<cloudApiNumber>?text=<URL-encoded 'Hola! Quiero la oferta #OFFERCODE'>. Keep the text under 140 characters. Meta's QR/short links provide no analytics, so the redirect is the only click measurement.

Identify the product with deterministic sources before any LLM step, in this order: (1) a regex for the #OFFERCODE in the first message, (2) context.referred_product.product_retailer_id, (3) an 'order' webhook from the cart. Only if all three are missing should the LLM do free-text or fuzzy catalog search, with retrieval over the database. Sync the Shopify catalog to a Meta catalog so that product_retailer_id equals the Shopify variant SKU or ID.

Model the sales conversation as an explicit state machine that the LLM steers but cannot skip: IDENTIFIED → VARIANT_CONFIRMED (ask size/color only for in-stock variants) → PRICE_STOCK_CHECKED (tool reads from the database; the LLM never states a price the tool did not return) → CUSTOMER_DATA (name, delivery phone, departamento, municipio/ciudad, dirección, barrio, references) → SUMMARY → EXPLICIT_CONFIRMATION (an interactive 'Sí, confirmar' button or an exact affirmative) → ORDER_CREATED (Shopify COD order through a tool with an idempotency key) → post-order message. Gate the create-order tool in code, not only in the prompt.

Ask for the delivery phone explicitly and store both wa_id/phone and the BSUID (user_id). Usernames and BSUIDs mean the inbound webhook may not contain a phone number, and the courier needs one for COD.
In Colombia, address messages are India-only, so collect the address as free text with LLM extraction followed by an echo-back confirmation, or with a WhatsApp Flow that ends in a summary screen.

A human-handoff tool plus a visible escape (e.g. 'escribe ASESOR') are required, not optional (Business Messaging Policy). Trigger handoff on user request, repeated misunderstanding, complaints or returns, an address that fails validation, or low extraction confidence. Pause the bot for that conversation while a human handles it.

Store group membership and clicks as append-only, idempotent event logs keyed by the provider event ID: GroupEvent(join/leave), Click, ChatStart(offerCode), OrderCreated, OrderDelivered/Returned. Derive current membership from the log. KPIs: join rate (joins/invites), net members, leaves per post and per day, clicks per post per 100 members, chats per click, confirmed orders per chat, delivered-COD rate per offer and per group.

Link rotator: a GroupInvite table (inviteUrl, capacity, softCap about 85–90% of the limit, full flag, active). The public /g/<campaign> endpoint sends people to the first active group that is not full. Refresh member counts from group events or manual admin input. Keep a backup co-admin in every group.

Treat posting cadence as an experiment rather than a known best practice. Start low, compare cohorts of groups at different cadences, and watch leaves per post and block/report signals. Cut cadence when leave spikes follow posts.

Do not let conversation data from WhatsApp (Business Solution Data) train or improve any third-party model. Confirm the Claude API data-use terms and put them in writing (the Business Solution Terms third-party service provider clause).
open_questions: What is the current member cap of a Community announcement group, and does it hide members' phone numbers from each other? A primary WhatsApp FAQ source could not be reached, which matters for the privacy of 50k customers.

The quoted text matches that statute: Art. 3(a) says "Autorización: Consentimiento previo, expreso e informado del Titular para llevar a cabo el Tratamiento de datos personales", and Art. 9 says "...autorización previa e informada del Titular, la cual deberá ser obtenida por cualquier medio que pueda ser objeto de consulta posterior". Art. 10 lists the only cases where no authorization is needed: (a) information required by a public or administrative body in its legal functions, or by court order; (b) public-nature data; (c) medical or health emergencies; (d) processing authorized by law for historical, statistical or scientific purposes; (e) civil-registry data. None of these covers marketing or existing customers, so the researcher's unchecked assumption is correct. Ley 1581 has not been amended on these points as far as known. Re-check against the Senado or Función Pública text before relying on it.

Decreto 1377/2013 Art. 7 (DUR 1074/2015 Art. 2.2.2.25.2.4) says authorization can be recorded in any format that allows later consultation. It counts as valid when given (i) in writing, (ii) orally or (iii) by the holder's unequivocal conduct, and it states: "En ningún caso el silencio podrá asimilarse a una conducta inequívoca." verdicts.evidence: The quoted Art. 3 sentence ("...no podrá ser contactado por parte de gestores de cobranza mediante varios canales dentro de una misma semana ni en más de una ocasión durante el mismo día") and the Art. 2 'canales que estos autoricen' wording match the known text, and both are written for debt collection. What remains open is whether the SIC applies the frequency and channel limits to advertising, either through Art. 5 'en los mismos términos' or through SIC Circular Externa 001/2024. I could not check this: no fetch or search was possible, and I have no reliable memory of an SIC statement that settles it. The conservative approach (at most 1 promotional message per day per person, only on the authorized channel) is sensible risk management, but it is not an established legal requirement.

Checked against the known text; fetch was blocked. The Ley 2300 Art. 5 parágrafo says that buying a product or service cannot oblige the consumer to accept commercial messages, except those strictly related to what was bought. It adds: "Cuando se trate de promociones para alimentar bases de datos, el consumidor deberá saberlo y aceptarlo de manera explícita." The same result follows from the finalidad principle in Ley 1581 Art. 4(b) and Art. 12(a). So the system can send transactional messages about an order (confirmation, delivery, COD payment) to the buyer. It cannot send promotions to that buyer without separate, explicit marketing consent.

I could not reach crcom.gov.co, sedeelectronica.sic.gov.co, garrigues.com or lloredacamacho.com (egress blocked), and search was exhausted. The overall picture is consistent with what I know: the CRC changed the RNE after Ley 2300 so it covers messaging apps and email, and the SIC issued a 2024 circular requiring suppliers to consult the RNE. The SIC URL slug supports 'Circular Externa No. 01 del 26 de junio de 2024'. I could not independently confirm these specific points: the 10 April 2024 date of CRC Res. 7356; the 'section IV' location; the rule that RNE registration equals revocation; and the rule that new consent dated after registration is required. The sanction list (2,000 SMMLV, 6-month suspension, closure) comes from Ley 1581 Art. 23. Consumer-law breaches enforced under Ley 1480 Art. 61 have their own scale, also up to 2,000 SMMLV. Treat c9 as plausible but unverified. The practical control is the same either way: check numbers against the RNE before each campaign.

sources.title: Circular Externa 1 de 2024 SIC (fetch blocked; the slug alone indicates the 26 June 2024 date)

verdicts.evidence: The Art. 23 sanctions match the known text of Ley 1581. (a) Personal and institutional fines up to 2,000 SMMLV at the time of the sanction, which can be imposed repeatedly while the breach continues. (b) Suspension of processing for up to 6 months. (c) Temporary closure if the ordered fixes are not made. (d) Immediate and permanent closure of operations involving sensitive data. The confirmation covers only the legal structure. I could not verify the 2026 peso figures (SMMLV COP 1,750,905; Decrees 1469/1470 of 2025; the Consejo de Estado provisional suspension; Decreto 0159/2026; UVT 2026 = COP 52,374). Holland & Knight and DIAN could not be fetched. Ley 1955/2019 Art. 49 does require sanctions set in SMMLV to be computed in their UVT equivalent, so the exact peso cap depends on that conversion. Treat 'about COP 3.5 billion' as an upper-bound estimate, not a verified figure.

The SIC press release and the Infobae article (29 Oct 2025) could not be fetched; both domains were blocked. Search budget was exhausted. I have no independent memory of Resolución 78138 of 2 Oct 2025 or of the COP 670M amount. The claim fits established SIC enforcement against telecoms for marketing contacts without authorization, but I could not confirm the number, date, amount, whether it was an appeal confirmation, or that WhatsApp is named.

The SIC and Presidencia pages, the X post and Infobae were not reachable, and search was exhausted. I could not confirm that the circular is numbered 002/2026, when it was issued, or its exact wording on groups, distribution lists and third-party or scraped databases. Two more points. The circular is explicitly about elections, and Colombia's 2026 election cycle (Congress in March, presidential rounds in May and June) is over by 2026-09-25. It is at most persuasive as to how the SIC reads Ley 1581 on WhatsApp groups; it does not bind commercial promo groups. The underlying rule, that adding someone to a group requires prior authorization, follows directly from Ley 1581 Arts. 4(c) and 9 (see c1 and c14) and is the stronger basis.

The quoted Art. 4(c) text (principio de libertad) matches Ley 1581: data may not be obtained or disclosed without prior authorization. Art. 4(f) (acceso y circulación restringida) says personal data other than public information may not be on the Internet or other mass-disclosure or communication media, unless access is technically controlled to limit it to holders or authorized third parties. The researcher's inference, correctly labelled as such, is reasonable: an ordinary group shows every member's number to all the others, which is a disclosure the consent must cover. No SIC decision specific to commercial promo groups was found or checked. A design that avoids this: WhatsApp Channels or Community announcement groups, where members' numbers are not shown to other members. That product behaviour needs checking against Meta's current documentation.

The claim matches the known text of Código Penal Art. 269F, added by Ley 1273/2009: "El que, sin estar facultado para ello, con provecho propio o de un tercero, obtenga, compile, sustraiga, ofrezca, venda, intercambie, envíe, compre, intercepte, divulgue, modifique o emplee códigos personales, datos personales contenidos en ficheros, archivos, bases de datos o medios semejantes, incurrirá en pena de prisión de cuarenta y ocho (48) a noventa y seis (96) meses y en multa de 100 a 1000 salarios mínimos legales mensuales vigentes." A caveat: criminal liability requires intent (dolo) and 'sin estar facultado'. Buying a list is a real criminal risk, but it is not automatically a conviction. The administrative exposure under Ley 1581 is the more certain risk. Fetch was blocked, so this was not re-checked against the Senado page today.

verdicts.evidence: The article mapping matches Decreto 1377/2013 as compiled in DUR 1074/2015. Art. 13, Políticas de Tratamiento, is 2.2.2.25.3.1. Art. 14, Aviso de privacidad, is 2.2.2.25.3.2. Art. 15, Contenido mínimo del aviso de privacidad, is 2.2.2.25.3.3. The policy must be written in clear, simple language and include: name or business name, address, email and phone of the responsable; the processing and its purpose; the holder's rights; the person or area that handles petitions and claims; the procedure for access, correction, updating, deletion and revocation; and the policy's effective date and the database's period of validity. The aviso de privacidad is used when the policy cannot be made available and must say how to reach it. Fetch was blocked, so the exact wording was not re-checked today.

missed.claim: Consumer-protection rules apply to orders the AI agent places (Ley 1480/2011, Estatuto del Consumidor). Arts. 46–50 cover distance and e-commerce sales. The seller must give its identity and contact details, the total price including taxes and delivery costs, the product's characteristics, and the payment and delivery terms before the purchase. It must also keep a record of the transaction and send a summary or confirmation. Art. 47 gives a derecho de retracto, generally 5 business days after delivery, for non-traditional or distance sales. The bot's final confirmation step and the order message should state these items. Ley 527/1999 makes contracts formed by data messages, such as WhatsApp, valid.

Transmission and international transfer to processors. The system passes customer personal data (names, phones, addresses) to Meta (WhatsApp), Anthropic (Claude API) and Shopify, all of which process it outside Colombia. Ley 1581 Art. 26 and Decreto 1377 Arts. 24–25 (DUR 2.2.2.25.5.1–2) require one of two things for sending data to encargados: a data-transmission contract with the required clauses, or the holder's authorization. International transfers must meet the SIC's adequacy rules. The privacy notice and consent text should list these processors and purposes.

The SIC has issued guidance on processing personal data with artificial-intelligence systems. My recollection is Circular Externa 002 of August 2024; the number and date were not verified this session. It stresses privacy by design, impact assessment, transparency toward holders and accountability. That is directly relevant to a Claude-based agent that handles customer names and addresses.

Some ordinary data-protection duties still apply. The company must adopt a written data-processing policy and a named area for handling claims. Claims must be answered within Ley 1581 deadlines: queries in 10 business days (Art. 14) and claims in 15 business days (Art. 15). Registration in the SIC's Registro Nacional de Bases de Datos is mandatory only above a size threshold (Decreto 090/2018: companies with total assets over 100,000 UVT). A small store may be exempt, but the other duties still apply.

Transactional and promotional messages must be kept apart. Under Ley 2300 (Art. 5 parágrafo), messages 'estrictamente relacionados con el producto o servicio adquirido' can be sent without marketing consent, but promotions cannot. The system should classify each outbound WhatsApp message as transactional or marketing. Only marketing messages go through the checks for consent, RNE status, allowed hours and frequency. The data model should record consent per purpose and per channel, as separate flags with a timestamp and the notice version.

verdicts.corrected_claim: Country code is 57, and mobiles are 10-digit national numbers (example 3211234567). In libphonenumber's current CO mobile pattern the 3xx ranges are 300-305, 310-319, 320-323, only 3241-3249 within 324, 3300 and parts of 333x, 350-351 and 370. The pattern also includes two non-3 ranges, 9101xxxxxx and 9408xxxxxx, so 'starts with 3' is a good heuristic but not exhaustive; use libphonenumber rather than a hand-written regex. The WhatsApp form is 57 + 10 digits. nationalPrefixForParsing '0([3579]|4(?:[14]4|56))?' strips 0 and the carrier-selection codes. The latest release is v9.0.40 (Sep 23, 2026). CO phone metadata was last changed in v9.0.6 (May 23, 2025), but the carrier data for +57 was updated later, in v9.0.17 (Oct 23, 2025).

missed.claim: Ley 2300 de 2023 ('Dejen de fregar') limits when and through which channels consumers may be contacted. Contact is allowed Monday to Friday 7:00-19:00 and Saturday 8:00-15:00, never on Sundays or holidays, and only through channels the consumer authorized, with an easy cancellation mechanism. Several implementers apply these hours to advertising messages as well as to collections; the stricter frequency limits (one contact per day, no multiple channels in one week) are written for collections. Promo broadcasts and bot follow-ups should respect these hours and a Colombian holiday calendar.

verdicts.corrected_claim: Automating consumer or Business-app groups through an unofficial client (whatsapp-web.js, Baileys, SendFlow-style tools) breaks WhatsApp's Terms of Service and risks a ban. The non-EEA ToS, which covers Colombia (effective Jan 4, 2021), bans 'illegal or impermissible communications such as bulk messaging, auto-messaging, auto-dialing, and the like' and 'any non-personal use of our Services unless otherwise authorized by us'. It also bans reverse engineering, creating accounts 'through unauthorized or automated means', and building software or APIs that work substantially like WhatsApp. The Messaging Guidelines (updated Sept 23, 2026) are narrower than the researcher's quote: they ban unofficial clients, bulk messaging, auto-messaging, auto-dialing or automation 'to harm WhatsApp or our users'. That is framed as adversarial behaviour, not a blanket ban. whatsapp-web.js warns that users may be blocked. Baileys discourages bulk or automated messaging.
verdicts.evidence: Opened the Open Terms Archive copies. missed.claim: Colombian data-protection law (Ley 1581 de 2012 and Decreto 1377 de 2013, enforced by the SIC) requires prior, express and informed authorization, with its purpose stated, before personal data such as phone numbers is used for marketing. DV Digital must be able to prove when and how each of the 50k contacts authorized WhatsApp marketing from DV Digital. Numbers collected only for delivering COD orders may not cover promotions. The SIC imposes significant fines. This limits Meta's 'general opt-in' allowance, which applies only 'as long as businesses comply with all local laws'. (Not verified against a primary source this session: Colombian government sites were blocked.)

Colombia's Ley 2300 de 2023 ('Dejen de fregar') limits consumer contact for commercial or collection purposes through messaging channels, including instant-messaging apps. It sets allowed hours on weekdays and Saturdays, bans Sundays and holidays, and caps how often a consumer can be contacted per week. Promo posting schedules and any outbound template campaigns to the 50k list should be checked against it with a Colombian lawyer. (Exact hours and frequency not verified here: sources blocked.)

Meta's current WhatsApp Platform pricing is per message. Non-template (service) replies inside the 24-hour window are free. Marketing templates are charged per delivered message at the recipient country's rate, here Colombia. So the private sales chat is almost free when the customer starts it through a wa.me or offer link. Any proactive outbound campaign to the 50k list through the API costs money per message and is subject to per-user marketing frequency caps and quality-based messaging limits. (From Meta's 2025 pricing changes; not re-verified this session because developers.facebook.com was blocked.)

Two legal ways to broadcast at scale hide member phone numbers, unlike regular groups: WhatsApp Channels, which any account including the Business app can create, and Community announcement groups, where only admins post. Either is a stronger default than many 1,024-member groups for a 50k audience, both for privacy and to reduce reports. Posting stays manual or semi-manual because neither has an official posting API. (Not re-verified this session.)

The Groups API endpoints in the Meta OpenAPI spec (/{group_id}/invite_link, /{group_id}/join_requests, join_approval_mode) show that even API-managed groups use an invite link with optional admin approval, not direct adds. For any group, adding people who did not ask to join is the main cause of reports and bans. Opt-in should be user-initiated (link or QR) and logged with a timestamp and source so there is evidence of consent.

gaps.question: What consent does each segment of the 50,000+ numbers actually have? For each segment, find the source (Shopify checkout, COD form, bought or scraped list, earlier WhatsApp chats), the date, the wording, whether it names DV Digital, whether it covers promotional WhatsApp messages, and whether proof is stored. Then, for the segment without valid marketing consent: can a one-time consent-request message be sent lawfully under Ley 1581 Art. 9/12 and Ley 2300 Art. 5 Par. 1? Which Meta template category would that message fall into (utility is probably refused, so marketing at about USD 0.0125)? What minimum Art. 12 content does it need?
gaps.why_it_blocks: Every topic points to this as the deciding fact, but nobody answered it. It decides whether any business-started message, group invite or template campaign is allowed at all. It sets the size of the audience that can legally be reached, the re-consent budget (up to about USD 625 per pass) and the consent data model (per-purpose and per-channel flags, notice version, timestamp, possibly Shopify's 2026-07 whatsAppMarketingConsent). Without it the recommendation cannot say 'use the list' or 'rebuild the list from scratch'.

gaps.question: Is the 1 October 2026 service-message pricing change confirmed by a primary Meta source? The change: free-form replies inside the 24h window are charged at the utility rate (Colombia about USD 0.0008 / COP 2.9455) after 1,000 free per number per month, and utility templates inside the window lose their free status. Which entry points still give a free window (Click-to-WhatsApp ads, the Facebook Page CTA, and possibly Channel or catalog 'Message business' taps, but not wa.me or QR)? Do messages sent from the Business app side of a coexistence number stay free?
gaps.why_it_blocks: The topics contradict each other. meta-cloud-api (C8, C10) says service replies are paid after 1,000 per month from 6 days from now. promo-group-patterns (missed) says service replies are free and the wa.me sales chat is 'almost free'. That changes the unit economics of the AI agent, which sends many messages per order. It also affects whether offers should push traffic through Click-to-WhatsApp ads instead of wa.me links, and it needs a payment method on file by 30 Sep 2026.

gaps.question: Do Ley 2300 de 2023 (the Art. 3 hours and Art. 5 advertising extension) and the SIC Circular 001/2024 RNE check apply to offers posted in a WhatsApp Channel or announcement group the person joined voluntarily (pull), or only to messages pushed to an individual? Which frequency rule actually binds advertising? The topics give three versions: 'once a week per channel', 'once a day and not several channels in one week', and 'unclear, written for collectors'. Operationally, how does a small supplier get access to the CRC RNE, through what interface (bulk or API), how often must it check, and at what cost?
gaps.why_it_blocks: The compliance gate for outbound messages (allowed hours, Colombian holiday calendar, frequency cap, RNE suppression) cannot be built or skipped without this. Topics disagree on the frequency rule: whatsapp-groups and meta-cloud-api say weekly, colombia-law says unresolved. Whether Channel posts count as 'envío de mensajes publicitarios' decides whether the chosen broadcast format needs the same controls.

gaps.question: On a real device in Colombia as of September 2026, which one-to-many formats can the WhatsApp Business app run, and how do they expose members? Specifically: (a) can a Community be created from the Business app; (b) is the Community cap still 2,000, and are numbers hidden in its announcement group; (c) can Channel admins see a follower list or phone numbers (whatsapp-groups g15 says hidden from admins, but its own open question says unclear); (d) are usernames live for +57 users; (e) has the monthly cap on messages to non-responders launched in Colombia, at what value, and does it apply to Business-app sends?
gaps.why_it_blocks: The broadcast recommendation (Channel, Communities, or regular 1,024-member groups) rests on these facts, and every one is marked unverifiable or contested. promo-group-patterns recommends Community announcement groups as a strong default, while whatsapp-groups says they top out at 2,000 and may not be creatable from the Business app. Exposing numbers in regular groups is also the main Ley 1581 disclosure risk.

gaps.question: Should the manually run broadcast surface (Channel or groups) and the Cloud API AI-agent number be the same number through coexistence, or two separate numbers? If a coexistence number is restricted because of group or Channel reports, does that restriction (quality rating, account lock, messaging-limit tier) also hit the Cloud API side and the portfolio-wide limit? Is coexistence available for +57 numbers, and what happens to wa.me links and catalog 'Message business' taps when the catalog belongs to a different number from the one running the Channel?
gaps.why_it_blocks: No topic assessed how far a ban would spread. The recommended design either puts the order-taking agent on the same number as the report-prone promo surface, or needs two numbers, a clear rule for which number the offer links point to, and a second Business Verification or display name. Coexistence availability in Colombia and the Groups API exclusion are both unconfirmed.

gaps.question: What is DV Digital's actual fulfillment stack: Dropi, which carriers, and which Shopify plan? Does Dropi's Shopify app import orders created through orderCreate or draftOrderComplete (and what does it filter on: gateway name, tag, financial status, sourceName)? Or should the agent create the order directly through Dropi's Colombian API (api.dropi.co, IP allowlist, cod_dane city mapping)? Is a cédula (dni) or distributionCompany required for COD guides in Colombia?
gaps.why_it_blocks: The last step of the core flow ('an agent places the order') is not defined. Integrator evidence shows Dropi picks up Shopify orders only after about 15 minutes, some orders never arrive, and much of the evidence comes from Ecuador or Mexico. The user never confirmed that Dropi is in use. Choosing between orderCreate, the draft path and a direct Dropi API call changes the data model (DIVIPOLA or cod_dane mapping, a cédula field) and what the agent has to collect.

gaps.question: Can a Dev Dashboard app on DV Digital's current Shopify plan read and write customer PII (names, phones, addresses) through protected customer data access? Which plans qualify ('Shopify, Advanced, Plus' vs 'Advanced, Plus')? Is the live store in the same Organization as the app, so that the client-credentials grant works, or will it return shop_not_permitted and require the authorization-code flow with expiring offline tokens?
gaps.why_it_blocks: If PII comes back null or the token grant fails, the agent cannot upsert customers or set shipping addresses, which breaks COD order creation. Legacy admin-created custom apps are no longer available after 1 Jan 2026, so a workaround is not guaranteed. Both findings are marked as sources disagreeing or needing a live test.

gaps.question: Does DV Digital's product catalog comply with WhatsApp's Commerce Policy (supplements, health or cosmetic claims, adult items and similar)? And for processors outside Colombia (Meta, Anthropic, Shopify, Dropi), what does Ley 1581 Art. 26 / Decreto 1377 Arts. 24-25 require: transmission contracts or holder authorization, SIC adequacy for the US, and the required wording in the política de tratamiento? Do Anthropic's API terms satisfy the WhatsApp Business Solution Terms ban on using Business Solution Data to train or improve other AI models?
gaps.why_it_blocks: These points were raised only from memory and never verified. A Commerce Policy violation can get the catalog or number restricted regardless of how clean the consent is, and the privacy notice and consent text must name the processors and cross-border transfers before any consent campaign goes out.

resultado.topic: Is Meta's 1 Oct 2026 service-message pricing change confirmed? Which entry points still give a free window, and is Business-app (coexistence) traffic still free?
resultado.summary:
Short answer: yes. The change is real and it is Meta's own. The free-reply picture in promo-group-patterns is out of date, and meta-cloud-api (C8, C10) is correct. One limit on this check: every Meta domain was blocked by the egress proxy, and the web-search budget was already used up. So I could not open developers.facebook.com myself. Everything below comes from verbatim copies of Meta's pages kept on GitHub (mirrors of the "Pricing for non-template messages" page, a mirror of Meta's changelog, and an evidence file with raw Meta snippets fetched on 2026-09-13), checked against BSP docs. For that reason no claim is marked high confidence.

What Meta's own text says:
(1) "Effective October 1, 2026, Meta will charge for service messages, which have not been charged since November 2024." Utility messages sent in reply inside an open 24h window are also charged from that date; they had been free since 1 July 2025. Meta's changelog dates the documentation to 10 September 2026 (entries #444, #447, #451).
(2) The free tier is also Meta's text, captured on 13 Sep 2026: "Every business phone number will receive 1,000 free service messages per month" and "Meta will only charge as of the 1,001st service message delivered each month". Unused messages do not roll over. The tier covers service messages only. Utility templates inside the window are charged from the first one.
(3) Service messages cost the same as utility messages in each market, with no volume tiers. For Colombia, the base utility rate from Meta's public pricing endpoint (read on 2026-09-21 and reported secondhand) is USD 0.0008 / COP 2.9455. Colombia is not on the list of markets whose rates change on 1 Oct.

Free windows: Meta names only two free entry points: Click-to-WhatsApp ads and the Facebook Page call-to-action button. The user must come from the Android or iOS app, and the business must reply within 24h. Meta says the 72h window is unchanged for message delivery. I found nothing that makes wa.me links, QR codes, Channels or catalog 'Message business' taps free entry points. Whether an Instagram profile button counts is also unverified.

Coexistence: Meta's onboarding page (as mirrored on 20 Sep 2026) says messages sent from the WhatsApp Business app "will continue to be free" and do not affect Cloud API windows or pricing. Meta changed the coexistence onboarding docs on 22 Sep 2026, and I could not confirm the pricing sentence is still the same.

Payment method: Meta's pages say to have a payment method on file by 30 Sep 2026, but they disagree on what happens without one. The pricing page says only the first 1,000 service messages a month get delivered. The non-template page implies service delivery stops altogether. Either way, replies can silently stop.

What this means for the AI agent: in Colombia a 12–15-message order chat costs about USD 0.01 (COP ~35–45) after the free 1,000. That is not free, but it is negligible next to Claude tokens. Where the free ad window really pays off is in making marketing templates free (USD 0.0125 each), not the replies.

claims.claim: Meta's own documentation confirms that from 1 Oct 2026 it charges per message for service (non-template) messages, free since Nov 2024. It also charges for utility messages sent in reply inside an open 24h customer service window, free since 1 Jul 2025. The change was added to Meta's docs on 10 Sep 2026 (changelog #444/#447/#451).

design_implications: Resolve the contradiction in favour of meta-cloud-api (C8/C10). From 1 Oct 2026, AI-agent replies are paid after 1,000 per number per month. In Colombia they cost about USD 0.0008 (COP ~2.95) each, so 'almost free' is still roughly true in practice, but the budget model must not say 'free'.

Unit economics: an order chat with about 12–15 outbound bot messages costs about USD 0.010–0.012 (COP ~35–45) in Meta fees after the free tier. The 1,000 free messages cover roughly 70–80 such orders per number per month. Claude API tokens will cost more than the WhatsApp fees, so tune the prompts and model choice before trimming WhatsApp messages.

Add a payment method to the WABA in Business Manager / Billing Hub before 30 Sep 2026, which is 5 days away. Handle error 131042 and alert on failed statuses; otherwise bot replies may silently stop once the free 1,000 are used, or from 1 Oct.

Inside an open 24h window, send the order summary and confirmation as free-form or interactive (service) messages, not utility templates. Service messages use the free tier first, while in-window utility templates are charged from the first one; after the tier the price is the same. Keep utility templates for after-window updates (shipping, COD delivery day).
Merge content into fewer, richer messages (for example product, price, stock and total in one interactive message with buttons). Every delivered message is billed on its own after the free tier.

Use Click-to-WhatsApp ads, or the Facebook Page WhatsApp button, for paid acquisition. They open a 72h window in which all messages are free, including marketing templates (USD 0.0125 each in Colombia) and utility follow-ups. That makes a CTWA-started chat the cheapest place for a same-week re-engagement or upsell template. The bot must answer within 24h and the user must be on the mobile app.

Keep wa.me links in the promo groups and group posts. They are not free entry points, but at USD 0.0008 per reply the cost is negligible. Do not move group traffic to ads just for message cost; do it only if you also want paid reach.

If you use coexistence (same number in the Business app and the Cloud API), a human writing from the phone app is free and does not open or extend API windows. The promo groups stay in the Business app, because group chats do not sync to the API. The AI agent works only in 1:1 chats through the Cloud API. Meta changed the coexistence docs on 22 Sep, so re-check the pricing section before relying on it.

Log pricing.type and pricing.category from every status webhook in Prisma, per order and per number. That lets you measure the free-tier burn and the real cost per order. Do not branch on pricing.billable, which is deprecated.

Keep rates in config (DB table per market, category and currency), not in code. Meta can change rates on 1 Jan, 1 Apr, 1 Jul and 1 Oct. Check which currency the WABA is billed in (USD or COP) before quoting COP figures.

resultado.topic: How much of the 50,000+ list has valid consent, and whether a one-time WhatsApp consent request is lawful (Ley 1581 Art. 9/12, Ley 2300 Art. 5, Meta template category, Art. 12 content)
resultado.summary:
SHORT ANSWER: Nobody can say from outside the business what consent each segment has. The owner has to supply it. The repo has no record of it: the DV Confirma Prisma model `Cliente` stores only nome/telefone/email/criadoEm. It has no source, date, notice-text or consent fields, and no lead import. The part that can be settled from the texts is the legal test each segment has to pass. The main finding is that the cheap "send everyone one consent-request template" plan fails on WhatsApp policy before Colombian law even comes into it.

WHAT EACH SOURCE TYPICALLY GIVES (owner to confirm counts, dates, screenshots and exports):
(1) Shopify checkout. The default labels are "Email me with news and offers" and "Text me with news and offers". The SMS disclaimer says "By signing up via text, you agree to receive recurring automated marketing messages...". Neither mentions WhatsApp, and neither label names the store, although the checkout page itself carries the store's branding. Shopify stores the consent state, timestamp, opt-in level and source for each channel (email, SMS). It does not store the wording shown. `Order.customerAcceptsMarketing` covers email only. A WhatsApp consent field (`CustomerPhoneNumber.whatsAppMarketingConsent`, mutation `customerWhatsAppMarketingConsentUpdate`) exists only from Admin API 2026-07 and defaults to NEVER_SUBSCRIBED. Result: at most SMS or email marketing consent, with no WhatsApp consent and no stored notice text.
(2) COD form app. I could not verify the vendors' features. Unless the form showed a separate, unticked marketing checkbox with the Art. 12 information, the number was given to get the order delivered. That is authorization for order messages only.
(3) Bought or scraped lists. There is no authorization toward DV Digital. Ley 1581 Art. 4(c) and Decreto 1377 Art. 4 forbid obtaining data without prior authorization. A mobile number is not "dato público". Even one consent-request message is unauthorised Tratamiento ("uso"), so there is no lawful re-consent path. The data should be deleted.
(4) Earlier WhatsApp chats. The customer started them, which is an unequivocal act authorising a reply (Decreto 1377 Art. 7) but not marketing. Marketing consent can be asked in the thread, for free, only when the customer writes again and the 24-hour window is open.

CAN A ONE-TIME CONSENT REQUEST BE SENT?
- Colombian law, own customers (segments 1, 2, 4): yes, arguably, if the message is strictly non-promotional. Decreto 1377 Art. 5 requires "una nueva autorización cuando el cambio se refiera a la finalidad". C-748/11 says any different use "deberá ser autorizada en forma expresa". Asking for that new authorization over the channel the customer already uses is the step the rule anticipates. I found no SIC concept that confirms or forbids it, so this is an interpretation.
- Silence never counts as consent (Decreto 1377 Art. 7; C-748/11).
- The legacy 30-day silence mechanism (Decreto 1377 Art. 10) applied only to data collected before 27 June 2013, so it is not available.
- If the message contains any offer, it becomes a "mensaje publicitario" under Ley 2300 Art. 5. That brings in explicit prior acceptance (Par. 2), an opt-out mechanism, the legal hours (Par. 3 → Art. 3: Monday–Friday 7:00–19:00, Saturday 8:00–15:00, no Sundays or holidays) and the RNE check (SIC Circular Externa 001/2024; registering in the RNE revokes earlier prospecting authorizations).
- I could not retrieve the text of Ley 2300 Art. 5 Parágrafo 1. The conclusion does not depend on it.
- WhatsApp policy (last updated Sep 23, 2026): "You may only contact people on WhatsApp if: (a) they have given you their mobile phone number... and (b) you have received opt-in permission from the recipient confirming that they wish to receive subsequent messages or calls from you." This applies to the Business App as well as the Platform. So any WhatsApp message, group add or template sent to a number without an opt-in to hear from DV Digital breaks policy, whatever it says.
- Meta's opt-in page (Jun 2026) allows a general, non-WhatsApp-specific opt-in if it names the business. So COD customers who agreed to receive order messages from DV Digital are reachable for order messages. A marketing-consent request to them is policy-borderline but defensible. It is not possible for the bought or scraped segment.

TEMPLATE CATEGORY: MARKETING. Utility "Opt-In Management" only covers confirming an opt-in already collected on another channel (website, email) or confirming an opt-out. Utility also requires the message to be non-promotional and specific to the user's order or account. Since April 9, 2025, a template submitted as UTILITY that Meta judges to be marketing is approved as MARKETING, and repeated misuse brings escalating restrictions.

PRICE: The ~USD 0.0125 figure may be stale. Meta publishes its per-country rates only as a CSV, which I could not open. A current BSP rate card (Gallabox, effective Oct 1, 2026) lists Colombia marketing at USD 0.0144, so one pass to 50,000 delivered numbers is about USD 720, not 625. Only delivered templates are charged.

ART. 12 MINIMUM CONTENT:
(a) the processing and each specific purpose (promo messages on WhatsApp, group invitations, ordering through an automated AI agent);
(b) that answering is optional, which is only mandatory for sensitive data or minors' data but should be stated anyway;
(c) the holder's rights (conocer, actualizar, rectificar, suprimir, revocar);
(d) the controller's identity, physical or electronic address and phone number.
Keep proof of the disclosure and of the authorization (Art. 12 par.; Art. 17(b); Decreto 1377 Art. 8). Add from Meta: state the business name and that the person is opting in to receive its messages. Add from Ley 2300: an explicit button to accept and an easy opt-out.

CONCLUSION: Use only the provable-customer segments, and only after each segment's source, wording and evidence are confirmed. Discard the bought or scraped segment. Collect consent mainly on channels the business controls: a WhatsApp checkbox in checkout or the COD form, in-thread when customers write in, and click-to-WhatsApp ads. Do not mass-template the full 50k.

claims.claim: The consent facts per segment are not recorded anywhere in the current system. The DV Confirma Prisma model `Cliente` has only nome, telefone (unique), email and criadoEm. It has no consent, source, collection-date or notice-version fields, and the repo has no lead-import path. So the source, date, wording, DV Digital naming and proof for each segment can only come from the owner: Shopify customer exports, COD-app settings and logs, and seller contracts.
